: end product of heme catabolism from senescent RBCs; Hgb → heme + globin; heme oxygenase (ER) → biliverdin; biliverdin reductase → unconjugated bili (bright yellow, toxic); 75% from reticuloendothelial system; other sources: heme proteins (cytochromes, catalase, peroxidase, myoglobin) & ineffective erythropoiesis

: unconjugated bili not H2O-soluble, bound to albumin → liver; UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1) adds glucuronic acid → H2O-soluble conjugated bili → bile → intestines → feces as urobilinogen & urine as urobilin
↑: Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, intrahepatic cholestasis, hepatitis, cirrhosis, sepsis, biliary obstruction (choledocholithiasis, sclerosing cholangitis, pancreatitis)
: MC inherited disorder of bili glucuronidation; benign, AR; ⇣ production of UGT1A1 → ↑ unconjugated bili; prevalence up to 14%; chromosome 2 (2q37), UGT1A1 mutation; ↑ risk of cholelithiasis
: type I = complete absence of UGT1A1 → severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia

: ⇣ excretory function of hepatocytes; benign, AR; conjugated hyperbilirubinemia; defective MRP2 transporter → impaired conjugated bili excretion; black liver; gallbladder not visualized on oral cholecystography

: ⇣ hepatic reuptake of bili conjugates; defect in hepatic storage/transport → mixed direct & indirect hyperbilirubinemia; benign, AR; ⍉ liver pigmentation; gallbladder visualized on oral cholecystography

: intermittent jaundice, otherwise aSx; triggered by stress, illness, physical exertion, hemolysis, fasting, menses, ETOH; scleral icterus & jaundice during acute episodes; jaundice also w/ intercurrent febrile illness

▪︎iron stored as hemosiderin in liver, heart, pancreas, pituitary, testes, kidneys, adrenals
▪︎onset of clinical dz typically >50yo, earlier in men than women; most identified before sx by liver & iron screenings
▪︎cirrhosis more likely w/ concomitant alcohol use d/o; can present w/ bleeding esophageal varices; ⇡ risk HCC
Early sx nonspecific: fatigue, arthralgia; later arthropathy, hepatomegaly, skin pigmentation, hepatic dysfunction, cardiac enlargement or failure, DM, ED
▪︎untreated → early death; w/ early detection & tx survival appears normal if ferritin <2,000 at dx
(low threshold for labs if suspected): serum iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation (TSAT), serum ferritin;
TSAT >40% & ferritin above ULN → excess iron stores
▪︎ferritin >1,000, evidence of liver injury, or cardiac injury → MRI to estimate body iron stores (liver, heart, or combined)
▪︎⇡ liver enzymes → liver bx to assess fibrosis & look for cirrhosis/other causes; bx shows intense iron deposits in hepatocytes w/ Prussian blue stain
if evidence of organ injury, significant iron on imaging, or ferritin >1,000: remove 1 unit blood over ≥2 hrs; start qweek for mild overload, more often for severe; target ferritin w/in normal limits
▪︎ferritin <500 & no tissue iron deposits → monitor yearly for ⇡ ferritin, TSAT, or progression
▪︎iron chelation alternative if also anemic or can't tolerate phlebotomy

▪︎⍉alcohol; HCC screening if cirrhosis; ⍉vitamins/supplements w/ iron; ⍉uncooked seafood (⇡ risk infection w/ siderophilic organisms — Yersinia enterocolitica, Listeria monocytogenes, Vibrio vulnificus)
Genetic abnl → impaired cellular copper transport
; AR dz of copper metabolism; copper accum in liver, kidneys, brain, eyes
▪︎young → liver dz sx, older → neuropsych sx; pts 5–35yo w/ hepatic dysfunction, neuro sx, psych sx; no ⇡ ferritin; often chronic hepatitis
(copper in cornea) = dark rings encircling iris; pathognomonic
▪︎neuro: tremors, emotional problems, difficulty w/ hand, dysarthria, parkinsonism; onset typically <20yo
: ⇣ceruloplasmin, ⇣serum copper (most copper deposited in tissue), ⇡urine copper
▪︎any pt <40yo w/ unexplained tremor or other involuntary movements → eval for Wilson dz
